source_caption:
One of the most devastating portrayals of mental illness ever put on screen. A Woman Under the Influence follows Mabel, a housewife whose increasingly erratic behaviour puts a strain on her marriage and family. John Cassavetes captures the emotional complexities of an ordinary family with such raw honesty, showing how difficult it can be for people to understand someone whose inner world they cannot fully comprehend.

Gena Rowlands delivers an absolutely extraordinary performance, bringing so much vulnerability, warmth, and pain to Mabel that it’s almost difficult to watch at times. There’s something deeply heartbreaking about the way she tries to connect with the people around her while constantly feeling misunderstood. It’s a performance that stays with you long after the film ends.

An essential piece of American cinema and an absolute classic for anyone who appreciates powerful, deeply human performances.

🎥: A Woman Under the Influence (1974)
Dir. John Cassavetes

source_details.title: A Woman Under the Influence
source_details.synopsis: A Woman Under the Influence is a 1974 American drama film written and directed by John Cassavetes, and starring his wife Gena Rowlands and close friend Peter Falk. Rowlands plays a housewife whose unusual behavior leads to conflict with her blue-collar husband (Falk) and family. The film was Cassavetes' seventh as director, and was produced and distributed independently of major studios like most of his other films. The movie exhibits a highly naturalistic style in acting and camerawork compared to most Hollywood films from the era.
